notes.title: 4 endings, 1 system for tracking them
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/0f6d672d81092bd3325a3a1d4a03a543ab002e27.png[/img]

[i]Did you know that Batora: Lost Haven has more than one ending?[/i]

The core of the [b]Batora: Lost Haven[/b] experience is not only the combat system based on its dualism, but also the narrative, which with its multi-branching allows the player to be the master of their own destiny. Make the choices you prefer and [b]get to the ending that best suits you[/b], with the possibility of increasing the longevity of the game thanks to the high rate of replay value. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/00f453ce77ac1f4bc98a6a51eca2768861af1e14.gif[/img]

Batora: Lost Haven, in fact, [b]has 4 different endings[/b] and with the latest patch that we released on PC and which will soon be available on consoles as well, we decided to highlight this aspect even more.

[h1]How to recognize narrative branches[/h1]
Every time you have an important choice to make you will have a precise and distinguishable signal on the screen, and sound effects will accompany you in understanding that you are faced with something important. We have also added two essential moments to help you understand how many endings you have unlocked.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/75fdc2ad8aed4ffa59e6956fa74a48df124e7d1d.gif[/img]

Once you've finished the game, a [b]pop-up will appear [/b]to tell you how many of the 4 endings you unlocked, reminding you that you still have more to unlock, depending on the number of your runs. Once you're back in the main menu, the one on the initial screen, where you can decide whether to load a game or play a new one, [b]you'll notice some lit-up mandalas on the bottom.[/b]

[h1]How to track unlocked endings[/h1]
We've added 4 mandalas that will light up and color based on how many endings you've unlocked by making your specific choices throughout the game. In this way you will have the possibility to know [b]how many different branches you have taken[/b] and how many times you have to finish the game again, with the aim of unlocking the other endings at your disposal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/7cbbc02493667acbb3bbb118667026dfb8a9ac70.gif[/img]

[b]Let's make a practical example! [/b]During the adventure you will come to unlock one of the 4 endings, making certain choices that will lead you to side with some rather than others (we won't give you spoilers!). At the end of the first run, the mandala in the lower right corner will light up, which will make you understand that you have unlocked the first ending. 

[b]What does it mean?[/b] That you are missing 3 more! The order of the mandalas will always be the same, so there won't be a correspondence between the symbol and the unlocked ending, but simply a numerical sequence.

[i]Had you noticed this? How many endings have you discovered yet?[/i]

notes.title: Limits are over! Let's uncap Batora: Lost Haven.
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/b06ffa84799b528eeabbd005328bb5503bdb1c46.png[/img]

We have arrived at the last in-depth analysis dedicated to [b]the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1506440/view/5891302324255933238]21.12 patch[/url][/b] with which we have made important changes [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1506440/view/3627118151101566740]not only to the combat system[/url], but also to the first hour of the game, adding [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1506440/view/3676659200147787761]total support to Steam Deck[/url] and also going [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1506440/view/3627118151142347281]to add a difficulty selector[/url]. While waiting for the patch to arrive on consoles in the coming weeks, here are more details on the technical improvements made to the PC version of [b]Batora: Lost Haven[/b].

[list]
[*] [b]Added frame rate uncap[/b] - On PC we unlocked the frames, deciding to play in two different modes. The first with the frame rate locked up to 240fps and with the vertical synchrony active, the second instead expects to be able to play with the unlocked (variable refresh rate), unlimited frame rate, autonomously choosing the fps limiter, but with the v-sync off.

[*] [b]Full Support 21:9 aspect ratio[/b] - On PC, Batora: Lost Haven correctly supports 21:9 (and 16:10) aspect ratio for both user interface and scene rendering.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/2ce484f6407ec51622bf4f2509d9f62ac7137fdc.gif[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]Added skip sequences[/b] - you can now skip all the cutscenes you want in order to speed up the gaming experience ([b]especially if you are doing a second run[/b] and have already watched all possible scenes). The dialogues, on the other hand, continue to be skippable manually, one by one. Only the game boot sequence the first time you start Batora: Lost Haven can’t be skipped. 

[*] [b]Full compatibility on Steam Deck [/b]- We have improved the readability of text throughout the game. When starting Batora: Lost Haven, the game runs in fullscreen mode at the [b]native Steam Deck resolution of 1280x800[/b]. Then, all the available features are now active on Batora: Lost Haven: the controller icons are now shown, the in-game interface text is legible and all functionality is accessible using the default controller configuration.
[/list]

This was the [b]latest update on our last patch[/b]. We trust that we have responded to all your feedback and respected all your requests. Our support for Batora: Lost Haven will obviously not end here and in the coming weeks we will continue to [b]keep you updated on the upcoming news[/b] regarding the game.

notes.title: Want a harder challenge? Now you can!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/0da6b01c33cd1915471d66e401cb14936e1e6ec6.png[/img]

You told us that you would have liked a difficulty selector in [b]Batora: Lost Haven[/b], so you can choose how to face your adventure with Avril. We have decided to listen to your feedback and insert 3 different degrees of difficulty, so as to allow you to adapt your adventure to your needs. 

We told you about it in our patch notes, but now let's go into more detail! To recover all the additions, you can check our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1506440?emclan=103582791469219169&emgid=5891302324255933238]patch notes[/url].

[i]None of the 3 difficulty modes will affect the acquisition of Trophies and Achievements. [/i]

[b]Before the patch[/b] - Batora: Lost Haven had only one difficulty level and attacks made in one nature (for example, physical) did 100% damage to the opponent of the same nature, instead a special coefficient was used to calculate the damage of the opposite nature, which was much less, but still present.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/99f8506b66983b2215666c9021a336490fdf9341.gif[/img]

notes.title: How we’ve improved Batora: Lost Haven’s combat system
notes.notes:
The combat system, together with the multi-branching narrative, is certainly the heart of the Batora: Lost Haven experience. Many of you appreciated the idea of dual nature, but we listened to your feedback in this case too by making changes to some aspects, so as to make the whole gameplay more dynamic and also more visually spectacular. Here are the major details regarding the changes made with the latest patch on December 21st.

[list]
[*][b]Intensity Feedback Impact [/b]- Visually we wanted to improve the impact that Avril's sword, or any other blow from her, inflicts on an opponent. Thanks to the Freeze Hit, once a mob is hit, it will suffer a backlash that will lead it to freeze on itself and interrupt the animation, as if it were, in fact, frozen. This aspect, already present in the game, has been enhanced to have a greater visual and more realistic impact. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/77388ac2647dbbb1d47c53e8a9e9840562124517.gif[/img]

To make all of this have an even higher value from a visual point of view, we added a more present camera shake: a VFX effect that is generated both in the zoom-in and in the zoom-out view, attacking both physically and mentally. At the same time, the SFX for physical and mental hits has been improved.

[*][b]Attack Queue[/b] - We've already talked about how we implemented a memory system for the combos you're going to perform, but we'll talk about it in more detail now. This means introducing a memory system that remembers the keys you press, no matter what strokes Avril is making. 
Pressing a key, on the other hand, is much faster than the action performed by Avril herself, so you will find yourself making combos with your key combinations that will go faster than how Avril can make her animations. For this reason we have ensured that the system can keep the next action in memory and loop all the animations following your instructions, without losing anything.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/25664a7b7a6beeb865016903e96c7686e64a60b1.gif[/img]

A practical example: if after dodging we want to hit immediately, the system will remember that you pressed the hit button immediately after the dodge button and will perform the animations in sequence.
[/list]

From your feedback, it emerged that the first hour of Batora: Lost Haven did not fully reflect what is the overall adventure which develops in the following hours. For this reason we have been working hard to make the first approach with Avril more dynamic and also [b]to modify the Oniric Arena[/b], following all your indications! 

After our latest post giving you an overview of everything that the new patch introduced, here is a greater detail regarding the changes made in the first hour of the game!
[list]
[*][b]Inside the Oniric Arena[/b] - the first version of the arena allowed you to defeat an enemy with one hit, no matter what nature you were in. Instead, now you will be able to engage in real combat against the enemies in the Arena, to be prepared for what the overall game will be. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/6f4eef1da11f922e15263cf2c8265fc4e852e95c.gif[/img]

Avril continues to be immune, therefore she will not suffer hits, but the fight must be carried out on a regular basis, therefore following the options of dualism. 4 to 5 strikes in both physical and mental nature will be required to defeat each enemy! We also decided to remove the skills, which were all initially unlocked, so that Avril can only use basic attacks, as well as in the first few hours of the game.

[*][b]The Oniric Arena[/b] - We have decided to change the appearance and setting of the Oniric Arena as well. We’ve replaced the huge square arena filled with ruins scattered around the perimeter with flying islands in the sky, from which it is possible to observe the planets below. In the background there will be infinity and waterfalls have been added, to enhance the feeling of a dreamlike environment. 

From an art direction point of view, we wanted to recreate an unconscious perception of Batora's power as she is trying to contact Avril. The Oniric Arena becomes, to all intents and purposes, an environment in which [b]space has no limits and time bends and takes shape[/b], so much so that all normal forces lose scientific coherence.
Thus Avril finds herself living an out-of-body experience, which ends up giving her the ability to perceive contact with Batora and see the planets in which she will face her adventure. She hears the screams, feels the power of Sun and Moon, and even understands the endless duel.

[*][b]After the Oniric Arena[/b] - From a gameplay point of view, we have decided to improve the pacing fight, with a balance that increases the duration of the fights, but always leaving you with that sense of power that distinguishes the first hour of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/25664a7b7a6beeb865016903e96c7686e64a60b1.gif[/img]

Immediately after the Oniric Arena, we also decided to balance [b]the first battles on Gryja more[/b], so as to make the gameplay experience more rewarding until the arrival of Carador.

Another aspect that we have decided to enhance is the reduction of tutorials during the game, to streamline the presence of text on the screen and make the gaming experience much more dynamic![/list]

notes.title: How we created Lunisolar Precession
notes.notes:
Nothing in the creation of a video game is random.

Behind every choice, behind every action performed by our protagonist, there is a design reasoning.
This also applies to Avril's most peculiar moves, such as the Lunisolar Precession.

[i]The astral form of Moon and Sun orbit around Avril to assist her in fight: equip the Aeternal Seeking rune, spend one Combo Point each Nature to summon [b]the power of Moon and Sun[/b]. They will heal you and fight anyone that comes close with their immense power![/i]

[center][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/14cc6b6c43658e5b035a7f601d96edb9a7a37542.gif[/img][/center]

This is the explanation we used in our tutorial to explain how to use the most powerful among Avril's moves, which brings together the power of the [b]Sun and the Moon to unleash an ancestral[/b] force capable of routing opponents and giving in Avril also an energy recovery. But what exactly is the [b]Lunisolar Precession?[/b]

[h1]The movement of Sun and Moon[/h1]

We were inspired by the precession of the equinoxes, also known precisely as Lunisolar Precession. It is the displacement of the axis around which the [b]Earth makes its daily rotation[/b]: the cause of the displacement is precisely the combined gravitational attraction of the Sun and the Moon, which causes a slow thrust on the rotation axis creating an oscillation in about 25,800 years. 

[center][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/b3073c0da1e11fe0da878c11d7798971bac2cdd0.gif[/img][/center]

The Lunisolar Precession in [b]Batora: Lost Haven[/b] is an ability that conveys both powers and that we wanted to represent with the motion of two spheres around Avril, which becomes our pivot, our Earth that prevents contact between the Sun and the Moon. In addition to being a spatial movement, for us, an Italian team that’s very attached to the literature of our country, [b]it also represents a quote from Dante[/b], about two identities that attract each other, but never manage to reach each other. 

[h1]The romantic point of view[/h1]

Dante Alighieri, the author of the [b]Divine Comedy[/b], called this phenomenon the “motion of the eighth sphere” and spoke of it in his masterpiece, citing a phenomenon capable of reversing the fleet of stars and bringing our world, infirm, back to its primitive condition, [b]capable of producing the "true fruit"[/b]. A concept full of romanticism also enriched by the meaning of the rune itself, Aeternal Seeking, inspired by another verse by Dante from the Divine Comedy: "Love, which permits no loved one not to love", one of the most famous verses of the poem and of all Italian literature.

[center][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/00761af900ecf2c23a62077ba63296ff7ad6b804.gif[/img][/center]

The verse tells the poignant [b]love story between Paolo and Francesca[/b]. Even in Hell, they are forced to chase themself to express their love: they fly like birds in the air, twirling around themselves without ever being able to touch each other.
Paolo and Francesca were killed when her husband discovered the feeling that her wife developed for Paolo: she could not be married or love anyone but her husband; however, it is her own love that compels her to do so, and reciprocates Paolo's sincere sentiment.

This is the romantic effort that we wanted to pour [b]into the experience of Batora: Lost Haven[/b], to enrich Avril's adventure with a narrative element that hides lore ready to be explored, drawing inspiration from our Codex and the narrative plot we have created for our first action RPG.


Want to find out more behind-the-scenes details of [b]Batora: Lost Haven[/b]? Join us in our [url=https://discord.gg/s9XgvaB4]Discord channel to interact at any time with the development team[/url]!

notes.title: Don't settle for a run: jump into the New Game+
notes.notes:
[h2]The story of Avril does not stop at the first run: the multi branching allows you to go and discover everything that Batora: Lost Haven can give you![/h2]

Let's start by saying that once you have finished your first run and defeated the final boss, which will be different depending on what you have chosen to do during your adventure, the [b]New Game +[/b] will be unlocked in the main title.

[h3]New Game +, what do you bring with you[/h3]

Batora: Lost Haven will start from the beginning and give you the chance to make the choices you didn't make in your first run. The UI will also come to meet you by indicating the choices you have decided to take earlier, so as to suggest what to do to change the course of events. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/43e1aa6681ec782a4ae16a3abe2395ea5e70574f.png[/img]

In this new adventure [b]you will keep your level[/b] and take with you the runes obtained from the quests, but not those that can be purchased in the shops. [b]All skills will be unlocked immediately[/b], which allows us to increase the level of difficulty.

In the event that you have reached the final boss by reaching the level cap of 25, in the New Game+ you will have [b]the opportunity to reach level 30[/b], with the progression that will be optimized and slowed down compared to the first run. [b]All mobs will follow your level[/b], so as to adapt the level of challenge and avoid that you can find yourself being too performing compared to your opponents.

[h3]The functioning of the runes in the NG +[/h3]

Starting the New Game + with all the skills available and also all the rune points on your side ([url=https://www.batora.game/2022/07/28/growth-system-runes-mechanics-batora-lost-haven/]do you remember how the rune system works?[/url]) will be useful to go to work on [b]an optimization speech of your build[/b], enhancing Avril with some tweaks which will be fundamental to face the second run. 

So if, for example, you have equipped a rune that increases the attack value by two points, but you still have some rune points to spend, you can buy the one that gives three more points of attack and equip it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/0038078c3debea0565c60eebde9422cb413fa733.gif[/img]

We remind you that Batora: Lost Haven [b]has two different final bosses[/b], depending on your choices, and two crossroads choices for each planet: [b]there are 4 endings[/b] in total and it is up to you to discover them all, to be able to truly consider yourself completists of the universe of Batora: Lost Haven.

notes.title: Batora: Lost Haven October Dev Update
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/6d2cda418f8e9640c37c4809ef5ef23e30846bf7.png[/img]

[h1]Hello Keeper of Balance! [/h1]

[b]The release date of Batora: Lost Haven is very close, so it’s time to reveal some new updates that you will find in the final version of the gameplay,  to explain to you what you are going to play.[/b]

[h2]Level Up and minor update[/h2]

[b]A new level-up reward[/b] - In our last update, we explained to you how to get a level-up in Batora: Lost Haven, but the time has come to tell you that we have decided to include the possibility not only to recharge both the HP bars of your life completely, but also to [b]introduce an area of damage[/b] around Avril that pushes enemies away from her. 

Leveling up thus becomes a really strategic asset within the combat system, which allows you not only to gain some healing, but also to take advantage of a second of stasis during very tight fights.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/06dea4a3c2143da24501199c57d1db7777602e90.gif[/img]

[b]Exploration reward[/b] - In addition to this level-up change, we have also decided to[b] improve the rewards that are granted by exploration.[/b] Now you have the opportunity to find runes in chests scattered around the environment so as in puzzles. 

[b]Fireflies speed increased[/b] - Among the exploration updates you will also notice that we increased the speed of the fireflies, to prevent Avril from overtaking them when you found yourself asking for a suggestion on the direction to take. Fireflies can be summoned to your support to show you the way to go to reach the next objective of the current mission.

[h2]Hybrid enemies and skill enhancements[/h2]

[b]Hybrid Enemies[/b] - We have placed a lot more emphasis on hybrid enemies. We are talking about opponents who must be fought both with the mental form and with the physical form, because they are vulnerable to both and not just one. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/0baa0c8b850f3b1ba1bde10800bed97ffac54339.png[/img]

With this update, hybrids [b]are promoted to the role of real mini-bosses [/b]and you will often find them defending dungeons within which puzzles to complete to advance in the game are hidden. A mechanic that will allow you to test your combat skills and then concentrate more on the logic required by solving the next environmental puzzle.

[b]Mental and Physical Shield edits[/b] - We improved the [b]AI ​​of all your opponents [/b]and at the same time some of Avril's abilities, to allow combat to be more dynamic and engaging. 

Let's start by saying that the mental shield was previously only blocking bullets, but now it is able to block any type of attack. As for the physical shield, we increased the defense value, although it is not yet able to totally cancel the damage.

[h2]Combo system changes[/h2]

Here, however, is the news that we most wanted to tell you about, because we have made some important improvements to the combo system. There will no longer be just one combo to unleash when you use your normal attack, but more sequences. 

Let's take an example based on the physical form: you will have your basic attack combo triggered by pressing the X button three times (in reference to an Xbox controller, or the Square button on a PlayStation console), or you have a different combo if you use the right stick of your controller. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/d7af48ca465038b6ca0d44c75b6a1b298e12b46b.gif[/img]

Instead of three normal blows, you will have [b]a regular blow followed by a lunge attack that will allow you to dash forward[/b] and decrease the gap with the opponent, from that moment, you can press the X button to deliver a sweep attack.

Within this system, another mechanism is also present, but this time[b] based on timing instead of input method[/b]. In fact, while attacking with the X button, if before the third blow you wait a little longer before pressing the action button again, a visual effect will be activated that will allow you to use another attack instead of the sweep, making Avril do a jump in the air with the sword and then land performing an area damage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/a999d442947e5e34ee86498a4e3e3cb4858914a8.gif[/img]

Using the same keys, therefore, according to your needs and learning to master the combo system at its best, you will be able to attack in different ways, so to change your offensive strategy and maximize results.

---

We can't wait to let you try this new combo system and to continue to tell you all the news of [b]Batora: Lost Haven[/b]!

Did this system intrigue you? Would you like to know more? Do you know we have a Discord channel that you can join and talk to the team whenever you want?

Remember to add [b]Batora: Lost Haven[/b] to your wishlist on Steam to not miss any updates regarding our project and to know all the news on the upcoming release!

notes.title: The rune mechanics in Batora: Lost Haven
notes.notes:
[h1]Hello Keeper of Balance! [/h1]

[b]In our last blog post we went to the discovery of all the updates about Batora: Lost Haven, but now it’s time to focus on what concerns the gameplay and some of the features related to it, specifically about the level up system and the rune mechanics.[/b]

We already know that in Batora: Lost Haven the action component will be very important, but today we want to focus on what will be the features related to the RPG: not only the level up system, but also the functioning of the runes, which will allow us to customize even more Avril and make our combat system even more layered.

[h2]How to Level Up[/h2]

Let’s start with the level up system, which is based on the accumulation of EXP points based on how many opponents we are going to defeat. Each mob will give you a specific amount of EXP points, which will allow you to level up even during a fight with a horde. We wanted to make it much more hardcore and block HP recovery as you level up: your stats will change, but you can’t rely on level up to recover energy. Keep this in mind! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/a05073ab61dbb20f6d3729dbf3747655a46cae81.gif[/img]
Avril’s level up

Obviously, in addition to defeating the monsters, Avril will be able to complete the main missions to accumulate EXP points and level up. We have already mentioned that Avril’s attributes will increase, so we specify that you will have both a physical and mental increase: HP and base attack value to start. The level up, however, will also bring another very important change from the point of view of the combat system: it will provide you with a new neutral rune point. And this allows us to enter the topic of the runes.

[h2]The runes mechanics[/h2]

Avril will always have the same weapons with her: to be able to customize them, and to also be able to customize Avril, we will have to rely on the runes. These will be both neutral and linked to the orientation of the protagonist, that can be both a defender and a conqueror. What do they mean? We will see it in more detail later. For now, just know that based on your karma you will accumulate rune points that will follow your balance, whether it is conqueror or defender, thus unlocking the possibility of equipping specific runes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/ec9a2780fc872c9eab27da60baa51ae6d6f8b17e.png[/img]
The Inventory with our runes equipped


A neutral rune will bring you only bonuses and no malus, but the former will be contained from the point of view of the advantages provided. With a Defender rune, however, as well as with a Conqueror, you will have a bonus which will correspond to a malus. Do you want some examples?

[b]Conqueror Rune[/b]: + 10% Critic Rate, -5% Mental Defense
[b]Defender Rune[/b]: + 10% Mental Defense, -5% Physical Defense

Then, each planet you visit will unlock new abilities. Avril begins her adventure, starting with basic attack and dodging, then she will learn the first pair of skills and so on, from planet to planet, for a gradual progression. In this phase of growth the runes will be fundamental, which will also add effects on the skills unlocked. Do you want some examples?

[h2]The Natural Boost[/h2]

After the first planet you will unlock an ability called Natural Boost, a mechanic that will enhance some of your abilities. When you unlock the shield, which will allow you to reflect the hits, with the right rune equipped during the Natural Boost (the rune called “Frangar, Non Flectar”) it will be possible to create an area behind the shield that will activate a recover of your HP, so you can not only reflect the blows of your opponents, but also find a moment of serenity to soothe your wounds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/c18cd3039aeb9b553dfa1521cdc27d4e6106e6bf.png[/img]
Frangar, Non Flectar – the shield ability improved by Natural Boost


It will be up to you to decide how to deal with your equipment and how to customize Avril, depending on your way of playing and how you are facing the adventure. This type of customization allowed us to avoid entering a skill tree that forced you to unlock skills that you would not have used with the sole aim of getting to unlock the next one. In Batora: Lost Haven you will have total flexibility in customizing Avril and your fighting style, creating a build that will satisfy you in all respects. Ensuring balance in the build is our priority from a gameplay point of view.

We can’t wait to be able to show you all the runes that you will have available in your inventory and let you find out how many mixes you could make thanks to this deep and customizable combat system. 

Did this system intrigue you? Would you like to know more? Do you know we have a Discord channel that you can join and talk to the team whenever you want?

Remember to add Batora: Lost Haven to your wishlist on Steam to not miss any updates regarding our project and to know all the news on the upcoming release!

notes.title: Life on Mahdzam - The Tribe of Fleki
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/a059729bad29109558f0129b4d44540add978765.png[/img]

[b]In our last lore blog we told you about the Yu Xuan tribe and more about the life on Huav. This time, we are going to tell you all about the Fleki tribe, that inhabit Mahzdam, one of the planets Avril will travel to during her journey in Batora: Lost Haven.[/b]

The [b]Fleki tribe[/b] live on a gigantic ark which contains numerous houses dug into the ice, a large market on the foredeck and a large place of worship on the aft deck. Every inhabitant of the ark is obsessed with the idea of ​​being able to "evaporate" and ascend to a higher life, and for this reason the ark's journey is always set towards the hottest places on the planet, following the cycle of the seasons. These journeys can last for months, and often the tribe of the ark orientates itself [b]thanks to the Northern Lights[/b] or small meteors in the sky, which always seem to guide towards the light.

However, hardly anyone is aware that the [b]Northern Lights[/b] are created by the souls of Huav's ascents after interrupting the cycle of reincarnation, and the meteors are nothing more than the stellar rains coming from [b]Gryja[/b].

[b]The Fleki civilization is nomadic[/b], and survives by hunting the primordials from the plane of Haf (ocean) thanks to large harpoons created from the fangs of the Rostungars (the walruses) and by collecting the primordial energies trapped inside the trees of Gler (the mirages). The second option is considered much more dangerous, as it requires the descent from the great ark, and for this reason it is carried out only by the most courageous and faithful to the law of the Trur (the faithful).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/b32d1abaf6f8ac5816a6e0b72fcb357aca0af7e4.png[/img]

The societal structure of the Fleki [b]does not include any kind of government[/b], and is totally based on the concept of the higher good, in which each individual always fights for the group, and never for himself. Precisely for this reason the sense of camaraderie and belonging is extremely developed on the ark, and each inhabitant is a proud individual and ready to sacrifice for the good of their people.

The only "guide" that the people of the [b]Fleki [/b]accept, excluding that of their captain, is linked to the great cycle of the vortex, since every inhabitant of the ark is aware that if he will drive out the evils of the abyss and will pray to heaven every day. one day it may become gas, thus deserving a rightful place among the Trur sages.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/38990da7c7dabdc4ca6c01740bec72f07d6aaf9f.png[/img]

We hope you’ve enjoyed learning about the [b]Fleki tribe of Mahzdam[/b]. We’ll be sharing more information about the world of [b]Batora: Lost Haven[/b] as we head towards launch this fall.

In the meantime, don’t forget to add [b]Batora: Lost Haven[/b] to your Steam Wishlist to keep up to date with news and behind-the-scenes content!

notes.title: Batora: Lost Haven Dev Update
notes.notes:
Hello, Keepers of Balance!

As time goes by and you’ve already had two chances to try the game - last Summer’s Closed Alpha and the most recent Demo during February’s Steam Next Fest, and each time you helped us by filling out some quite detailed feedback forms that contributed to the game’s improvement, it’s only fair that we share with you the details of how the game has improved since the closed alpha and what we’ll keep doing to improve it until it launches, later this year!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/412ad2e0f0402e39be0e56ea60b75131a2c7a07f.jpg[/img]

[h2]Updates since the Closed Alpha[/h2]

Last Summer’s Closed Alpha was the first real taste of Batora: Lost Haven for players. Over 23k gamers got a key to try it and the response was AMAZING!

Seeing how many people played and enjoyed it made us super proud, especially since you appreciated it so much even at such an early stage of development.

That time, your feedback was extremely helpful as it pointed out some issues that we were aware of and some that made it clearer what kind of game you envisioned Batora: Lost Haven to be.

So, besides overall performance enhancement - remember that it was in alpha stage - following are the main updates we implemented since the Closed Alpha:

[b]Camera system and navigability[/b]
As some users pointed out that the camera movements would cause motion sickness, we improved the camera system and level design for a better level legibility

[b]Enhanced controls (focusing on keyboard and mouse)[/b]
We improved the animation system, the combo windows, and overall responsiveness of the controls 

[b]Impact on physical hits[/b]
We introduced the camera shake and freeze on hit and improved the attacks’ VFX to ensure that physical hits would give the right “impact” feeling

[b]Progression feedback[/b]
We improved the in-game notification system and the VFX for level-up and acquired items, to highlight in a more incisive way whenever players reach a new level or get runes or new skills

[b]Strategic combat boost[/b]
We improved the combat system in terms of AI and skills to make it more fun and strategically interesting

[b]Enemy spawn system[/b]
We improved the enemies’ spawn system to allow management of specific spawn points, increasing the fights’ variety and making them more “choreographic”

[b]New improved puzzles[/b]
We re-designed puzzles and VFX to be more accessible and clear; we also improved control sharpness

[b]New companions mechanics[/b]
We made the companion a part of the gameplay, so it now has an active role in fights too


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/f3f8d4f24a042936702d7d8bdfd7b422aa447c41.jpg[/img]

[h2]Work-in-progress updates for final release[/h2]
Then there was the Steam Next Fest: one intense week during which Steam users got to play the demo of Batora: Lost Haven and give us their feedback once again.

We’ve already started working on the new updates so that, as we head towards launch, everything will be ready and functional.

Here are the main features we’re working on:

[b]Zoom system[/b]
As many players pointed out that it would be great to be able to zoom on the beautifully detailed environments, we are implementing a system that allows players to adjust the camera choosing between 2 zoom modes 

[b]Pad controls[/b]
We’re improving the control system to make it more accurate and responsive to the player’s intentions, consistently adapting to the different control systems

[b]Reworked UI & menus[/b]
We re-designed the menus to make them clearer for players, showing relevant information and making it more accessible

[b]Codex[/b]
Players specifically asked to delve into the game’s plot and backstory, so they will now get to collect the codex pages while playing, thus learning more about the game’s lore

[b]New tutorials[/b]
We’re re-designing the tutorials to make them readable on all platforms. Players will be able to access them through the codex after unlocking them in-game.

[b]Full control customization[/b]
We’ll give users the possibility to customize the controls choosing their favorite bindings

[b]Rune stats[/b]
We’re improving the rune system, making their effects more impactful and remarkable 

[b]Improved health bars status[/b]
We’re adding a “semi-death” status to alert players when one or both of their health bars are below 20%

[b]Dubbing[/b]
As players were not convinced about some of the dubbing, we’re going to replace some actors - including Batora! - choosing the most appropriate ones for their roles

[b]Super detailed world-building[/b]
We’re adding more dialogs based on the players’ choices and their consequences - for example, characters and NPCs will talk in real-time commenting on what’s happening in the game

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/99d40b17bf0c9b21f634f8a435781452fd33a75e.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Shaping Up the Universe of Batora: Lost Haven – Mahdzam’s World Building
notes.notes:
Avril will explore some unique locations on her interplanetary journey! Today, we’d like to tell you more about the water planet – Mahdzam.

Mahdzam is shaped much like an inverted pyramid and is composed entirely of water which is present in liquid, solid and gaseous states.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/de06c727a0e0e66d09156b37e94ec570165d36e3.jpg[/img]

The base of the planet is a gigantic ocean inhabited by creatures which have shapes similar to newts and nagas. These beings are known as the Dirs (the Dir tribe) and are renowned for their ferociousness.

The liquid part of Mahdzam is the largest and is home to hundreds of life forms! Thanks to its proximity to the planet Lume the ocean receives a constant influx of heat, evaporating the water up to the sky, creating a giant gaseous vortex at the top of the pyramid.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/fdbc972e1a2b637e20072da5a51ce80d50e027f4.jpg[/img]

The middle of the planet is composed entirely of ice and is inhabited by the Flerki, a people made of penguins (Synir) and anthropomorphic walruses (Rostungar) who live inside a huge ark. This icy landscape has a totally flat shape and at the extreme limit of its borders, the ice falls towards the ocean below – converting back to liquid form in a continuous cycle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/73438e5f0e37b3d7494ec22c8b30a1a3efc0913c.jpg[/img]

The flora on Mahdzam is almost completely made of water too! It’s also not uncommon to see trees made entirely of gas, these are called Gler. The Gler are revered by the people of the ice, as they represent a link between them and the sages of the skies.

Because of its ‘inverted pyramid’ structure, Mahdzam has the complete opposite shape to the planet Huav, where the vortex is at the bottom. However, despite its substantial difference, Mahdzam also requires constant energy from the world of Lume to be able to sustain its continuous cycle. As a result of sharing the heat from the planet of fire, the planet suffers from very unstable periods, just like its counterpart.

notes.title: Life on Huav: The Yu Xuan Tribe
notes.notes:
[b]In our last blog, we told you all about the builders of Huav – the cunning and magical Xiaias. This time, we’re going to tell you about the other tribes that inhabit Huav – the powerful Yu Xuan, and their subordinate tribes, the Jingren and Congmin…[/b]

Wanmei is the jewel of the planet of Huav and is the place where all the wise cultures of destroyers live, holders of the power and eternal wisdom due to the proximity to the core and the immortal forest of Yulin. Wanmei's wonderful temples are the seat of the Yu Xuan, the wise holders of the world's wisdom. 

In fact, unlike Gryja, where the ruling class is represented by the builders’ faction, in Huav the destroyers, represented by the Yu Xuan, hold the power.

Their temples are created with the rarest and most precious materials on the planet and are used as both places of worship and political headquarters for the most important and wealthy exponents. 
The Yu Xuan are the sages who rule the energies of the winds. These have the task of communicating with the guardian through ancient rituals related to the music of the winds and are the only ones able to cover institutional positions. There is no way to ascend to this rank other than by birthright, so power plays are extremely common even among members of the same elite! Although they can live for a long time, their thirst for power has led them to monopolize the rains coming from the jade forest, making them almost immortal and extremely selfish. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/b78a44ac3638dce885851086abf2a2366b02c555.jpg[/img]

The Jingren are the elite guards of the realm and are the only ones who can carry weapons and armor! They are very tall, slender and extremely strong in combat. Each of them carries a cloak and glyphs that link them to one of the realm's temples, which helps them reveal their status and importance. Some of the Jingren are so powerful that they are able to manoeuvre (with the aid of coercion) some of the lesser Yu Xuan. This allows them to hold some sort of power behind the throne, yearning one day to be able to carry out a coup and subvert the status quo. According to their ancient tradition, the Jingren are born from the feathers released by the guardians during their journey, which is why their pride and arrogance is equal only to that of the Yu Xuan. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/659e970aad30e687f04b7f45cc4930de2e254bf8.jpg[/img]

The Congmin are the humblest bloodline that inhabits the Forbidden City and are the most common sub-culture. They usually perform roles as merchants. Although they are clearly less important than the priests or guardians, the Congmin are still part of the upper circle of the planet of Huav, which is why even the humblest of them wears extremely complex and precious clothes. The wealthier a Congmin is, the heavier the jewellery and items it wears. Their beak is longer than their counterparts and they have small lively eyes combined with long claws, useful for precision manual work!

We hope you’ve enjoyed learning about the different tribes on Huav. We’ll be sharing more information about the world of Batora: Lost Haven as we head towards launch next year.

notes.title: Life on Huav: the Xiaia Tribe
notes.notes:
On her journey across the planets, Avril will explore the breathtaking planet of air known as Huav. 

Huav is built on a huge hurricane, and its sharp rocks, apparently heavy, can float like clouds!
The planet is divided into five different realms, but only two of them are inhabited by superior physical beings: the builders, who call themselves Xiaia; the destroyers, who hold the power on this planet, are the Yu Xuan.
Today we’re going to tell you all about the Xiaia tribe!

Xiaias inhabit the desert of Huav, and they are cold-blooded beings, living in small slums made of debris scattered throughout the desert. During the night and in the hottest hours, the small lizards hide in the sand, avoiding unwanted contact with the primordials that infest the land during the most dangerous moments.

Xiaias are divided into two macro categories: the explorers and the shamans. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/98466e6812b49ef1b2c4f46d4534490d58102743.jpg[/img]

The explorers are nimble and cunning and instinctively capable of building small engineering masterpieces. Only the most capable explorers can climb the nets along the lower realm and so they are normally respected and revered by all! Explorers are often armed with bows or small swords made from scrap metal salvaged from the sky and wear improvised armor made from a mixture of metals and organic components. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/b368c5381348a91f10d45e8be571df1636090057.jpg[/img]

The shamans are smaller in size and have greenish skin. Unlike the explorers, these little lizards have a predilection for magical techniques due to a primordial instinct that allows them to understand and convey the winds and energies of the sand! In ancient times, the shamans were the only ones able to communicate directly with the guardians, and it was their job to calm the winds and keep the peace on all kingdoms…

Next time, we’ll introduce you to the other main tribe of Huav – the Yu Xuan, and their subordinates, the Jingren and Congmin.

notes.title: The hidden meaning behind the amulet on Avril's forehead
notes.notes:
The symbol on Avril's forehead certainly doesn't go unnoticed, but what is its hidden meaning? All right, it's time to reveal it!

First of all, this symbol is an amulet donated to Avril by Sun and Moon, the two mystical entities that lead her to start her quest to bring Earth back to its former glory, and it's the point from which Avril's mental power is released.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/c690227176452061b22acb27320fa280a2660d07.png[/img]

The primary source of inspiration for its design was the Egyptian creation myth:
Once there was nothing but endless dark water without form or purpose until one day, out of darkness and swirling chaos, the universe took shape and the first deities, the Earth god Geb and the sky goddess Nut, gave birth to Isis, Osiris, Set, and Nephthys and created life itself.

The reason behind the choice of this particular reference can be found in the message we wanted to convey, which is the opposition between the concepts of origin, life, and rebirth and that of chaos. At the same time, the shape of a Sun and a Moon aims at amplifying the idea of equilibrium between opposite and complementary forces thanks to which the universe was created and continues to exist.

The celestial bodies have intrigued humanity since the primordial times. Our ancestors observed these marvels of nature keenly and used them to explain the origin of life itself and understand its logic. The Sun and the Moon, more than any other heavenly object, were considered to be the center of human existence for a very long time.

The Sun and the Moon can represent even wholly different things in different cultures, but the one thing that they always have in common is their polarity: light and dark, day and night, male and female. The Sun is the realm of day and the waking hours' self, and the Moon inhabits the landscapes of the soul, emotions, and dream life. But we should never forget that their existence depends on each other despite them being opposites.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/f202900c096715706d2a56f91dbed9375782c5ea.jpg[/img]

The Moon has many different meanings. Usually, it stands for wisdom, femininity, knowledge, understanding, completion, death, and rebirth, and quite often, it also represents the rhythm of time. The Moon's phases symbolize immortality and eternity, enlightenment, or the dark side of nature herself.

Many well-known mythologies and religions feature the Moon as a goddess, including the Greek goddess Artemis, the Roman goddess Luna, the Egyptian goddess Isis and the Chinese goddess Chang'e. However, there are some exceptions: Sin of the Mesopotamians,
Mani of the Germanic tribes, Tsukuyomi of the Japanese, Igaluk/Alignak of the Inuit, and the Hindu god Chandraare are only some of the male lunar gods spread across the globe!

On the other hand, the Sun is a symbol of power, growth, health, passion, and life. In antiquity, it was frequently viewed not as simply a physical phenomenon but as a god, mainly for the ability to create life and making crops grow to sustain villages. In some cases, this divine Sun was also closely tied to an earthly ruler's power and assumed divinity, such as a king or pharaoh.

Last but not least, the color and position of the amulet are clearly inspired by the Hindu sixth chakra, the Ajna or Agya. The Ajna symbol is located in the center of the forehead between the eyebrows and it's also known as the third eye. It's believed to govern our ability to understand, perceive, and see beyond what lies in front of our eyes. The third eye is the source through which we can gain a higher understanding of reality, guiding us in our actions and choices. When this chakra is activated, it is believed to amplify the power of our minds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/f22ff764970a6312fd3e7e6338c8598925af6c94.jpg[/img]

While there are variations in the color of Ajna, this is usually indigo/purple, the meaning of which is often associated with wisdom, mystery, and faith.
The blazing purity of the Sun and the ever-flowing wisdom of the Moon fight by Avril's side and will be the key to restore and preserve universal balance. But don't think that is going to be a breeze!

Everything in the universe of Batora: Lost Haven is driven by opposing forces whose boundaries may be so blurred sometimes that their difference ceases to exist. It's up to you to decide whom to trust. So buckle up; you've got quite a long journey ahead of you!

notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

With the Batora: Lost Haven Closed Alpha just around the corner it is time we get deeper into what you can expect to see and the adventures you’ll be facing! There is a lot of exciting content to be shared with you, but this is still only a slice of the adventures you will face in the final game in 2022. Today’s post will be detailing all about where the Closed Alpha will be set, what places you will be able to visit, characters and enemies you’ll encounter and more. 

[h2][b]CLOSED ALPHA AND HOW YOU CAN GAIN ACCESS[/b][/h2]

Any one and everyone has the chance to sign up for the closed alpha, all you have to do is head over to this link and sign up for the Batora: Lost Haven newsletter! It is that simple! However, there isn’t much time left! Sign-ups close on the 20th July at 4PM CEST/3PM BST and the alpha will begin shortly after on the 21st July! 

Click [url=https://bit.ly/Batora-Alpha-Steam]here[/url] to sign up to the closed alpha!


[h2][b]PLANET GRYJA[/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/83e7e7af0abb1ed1d5cc683974d76db4fab8bd0a.png[/img]

The journey will begin in Gryja, the first of four planets in Batora: Lost Haven. Gryja is a desert planet that experiences reoccurring earthquakes, also known as Gryjaquakes. The planet consists of rocky grounds and despite Gryja’s settings being dry and desertic, its predominant colours are acidic! Which is why the glowing planet is filled with colourful fauna and crystals.

Life on Gryja follows a continuous life cycle, similar to reincarnation. Everly life form on the planet is destined to return to the planet’s core in which it will soon after form into a physical being again until it has been destroyed which then it will repeat the cycle. 


[h2][b]COMBAT SYSTEM[/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/709a6aa260c89412406210be57ddd91be1a51c02.png[/img]

The combat system in Batora: Lost Haven heavily focuses on the balance of duality. You’ll be playing with two abilities; Physical and Mental, this is called the Nature Switch. Each ability has its own mechanics and skills, this is reflected in their different play styles: Hack and Slash for the Physical ability and Twin Stick Shooter for the Mental ability. 

Nature Switch, however, is not limited to combat, it can also be used when interacting with various environmental elements, to solve puzzles and to help uncover hidden secrets. 


[h2][b]KARMA SYSTEM[/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/10e952524a5135cc76a6c2d8041cdaf4082e43b7.png[/img]

In Batora: Lost Haven you will have to make decisions that will decide Avril’s fate and how the game will end. This is called the Karma System.

Each planet will have many opportunities where you will have to make choices based on your own morals. Larger events and choices will affect the story and gameplay while others will change the behaviour of other minor characters that you will encounter.


[h2][b]CLOSED ALPHA FAQ[/b][/h2]

[b]WHAT REGIONS IS THE CLOSED ALPHA AVAILABLE IN?[/b]

The Closed Alpha will be available to newsletter subscribers from all over the world.

[b]WHAT LANGUAGES IS THE CLOSED ALPHA AVAILABLE IN?[/b]

The closed alpha is currently only in English (audio and subtitles). However, there will be many more languages added in for the full launch in 2022.

[b]CAN I TALK / POST / CREATE CONTENT ABOUT / OR STREAM THE CLOSED ALPHA?[/b]

Content creators are more than welcome to capture footage for content as long as it is stated that this is only the alpha and not the final game. It is still subject to improvement and change. 

[b]WILL MY ALPHA PROGRESS BE CARRIED OVER TO LAUNCH?[/b]

When Batora: Lost Haven is fully launched in 2022, all previous progress from the alpha will unfortunately be lost as the alpha doesn’t take place at the beginning of the story. There is much more for players to experience in the full launch!

notes.title: Shaping up the Universe of Batora: Lost Haven: Huav's World Building
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/02ef4a7ce07a67a3691efa636759ed99a9061a60.png[/img]
Today, we move forward to the world-building process of the next planet Avril will visit, Huav!

Huav is the planet that hosts the elemental essence of the air. Built on a huge hurricane, its sharp rocks, apparently heavy, can float like clouds.

The planet is divided into four different realms, called Lǐngyù, each having its own different culture, purpose, and origin. Generally, it is not possible to travel from a Lǐngyù to another due to the very strong updrafts and this has led to the establishment of a clear-cut class system in which the place of birth will determine one's social status almost forever.

Unlike Gryja, where the ruling class is represented by the builders’ faction, in Huav the destroyers, represented by the Yu Xuan, hold the power. 
 
When we came to design this world, we started by taking inspiration from existing planets, just as we did for Gryja. In the very beginning, Huav was indeed inspired by Neptune. However, the more we worked on its design, the more we moved away from this reference!

For the making of its realms, we took a lot of inspiration from Asian folklore and mythology. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/74a8ce1015a6ab8904973e626e691820beab72ed.jpg[/img]

In particular, Marco Polo's travel along the Silk Road, a network of ancient trade routes that connected Europe with the Far East, and the parallel ocean trade, which had existed for centuries depending on seasonal monsoon winds, strongly influenced the way we shaped the planet’s appearance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/9d65226836fac75e3c40a58fe6c5f84d6292d704.jpg[/img]

This is why, on Huav, you can find many traits of the East of the world's environments and cities, from the Great Indian Desert to the motifs and decorations of Imperial China, from the rainforests to the mountain range of the Himalayas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/2b1f958f04aea7796d5f8d462c08d74f13333fbb.jpg[/img]

Last but not least, one of Huav's four reigns is based on Black Rock City, a temporary metropolis in Nevada's desert where people gather to celebrate community, art, self-expression, and self-reliance once a year!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/11dc5895b98e6d7a91c50593c7da183a271a1e7c.jpg[/img]

[b]Keep following us to find out many other juicy details on the Universe of Batora: Lost Haven and make sure to wishlist the game![/b]

notes.title: Life on Gryja: The Destroyers
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/44397ea5d171b108b3c3267ffde5bc45fd385ac1.png[/img]

In the latest issues of Life on Gryja, we told you more about the two tribes that together form the Builders’ faction. 

Now, it’s finally time to reveal more details on their sworn enemies: [b]the Destroyers![/b]

As you might remember, Gryja’s life cycle is sustained by the primordial stream that flows from the planet’s central core throughout its entire surface, disseminating souls on the ground that later blossom into living essences that range from non-sentient to superior beings.

The experiences collected in the previous life and the quantity of terrestrial energy assimilated during one's cycle influence the level of consciousness these creatures have. Based on that, they are classified into primordial, intermediate, elevated, and guardian. 

[b]The destroyers of Gryja are almost exclusively composed of primordials.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/3ede93e73c1b99d47748165d7a54b631ec278f18.png[/img]

Primordials have little intellect and are mostly driven by survival. Their language is so underdeveloped, that they only communicate with simple sounds and with wide and slow gestures. Their primal instincts require them to constantly seek nourishment and new energy sources, which is why they continually attack builders' outposts and constructions. 

Their low sense of society, deriving from the previous experience of their essence, is the main cause for their nomadic lifestyle. While Builders have a great sense of community, Destroyers gather only in small tribes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/fa1c83473d6b263049a5567921407c40de6fd759.png[/img]

In the first entry of life on Gryja, we looked into the first tribe that lives on the planet, the Buna. Now, it’s time to move on to the next one, the Sakhras!

[b]The Sakhras, together with Buna, form the Builders’ alliance,[/b] whose oath is to protect their home, the village of Alhaya, against the threat of the Destroyers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/dad9f9f3d0bb2e966a6d257ef1f57ecd352260b6.jpg[/img]

The Sakhras are among the most recent forms of life on the planet of Gryja. Their toad-like appearance is linked to the fact that, unlike all other life forms on the planet,[b] their soul has remained partially bound to the liquid and fumes of the primordial stream. [/b]

Normally, Sakhras are much smaller than Buna, but some of them manage to grow to enormous size by eating a gigantic amount of raw crystals. The assumption of which, however, can be extremely dangerous and even leading to madness!

[b]The desire to "get fat" is tied to an internal social status[/b], and it is no coincidence that most dominant Sakhras tower over their smaller counterparts.

Even though they are tolerated by the Buna, the Sakhras are considered inferior, since they are not totally tied to the soul of the earth and are usually weaker than them. Despite this, however, [b]they managed to create a small empire, thanks to their keen intelligence, talent for machinery, and ruthless sense of business. [/b]

notes.title: Life on Gryja: the tribe of Buna
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/65442a87f985edb2edc3944909f18a8387090972.png[/img]

During the course of her interplanetary adventure, Avril will explore four different planets inhabited by the most diverse and fascinating creatures. 

Some of them will be peaceful while some others will be very dangerous.[b] Today, we’ll tell you a little bit more about those who inhabit Gryja, the first planet she will visit![/b]

[b]Life on Gryja follows a continuous cycle similar to reincarnation. [/b]Every single form of life is destined to return to the planet's core in the condition of a stellar particle and then form again and again. 

[b]This process is sustained by the primordial stream that flows from the planet’s central core throughout its entire surface[/b], disseminating souls on the ground that later blossom into living essences that range from non-sentient to superior beings.

The experiences collected in the previous life and the quantity of terrestrial energy assimilated during one's cycle influence the level of consciousness they have, based on which they are divided into primordial, intermediate, elevated, and guardian. These, in turn, are deployed in [b]two main factions that fight against each other: Builders and Destroyers.[/b]

Builders are the most advanced society on the planet and incorporate the races of Buna and Sakhra, who have joined forces to protect their village, Alhaya, from their sworn enemy, the Destroyers, a nomadic tribe who continually attacks builders' outposts and their constructions.

[b]Their alliance, however, does not prevent them from internal conflicts[/b]: despite possessing an extremely complex intellect and culture, the builders of Gryja are indeed deeply tied to a tradition based on strength and honor, and this leads to numerous episodes of social tensions and racism.

[b]Let’s discover more about the first of these two tribes forming the builders’ alliance: the Buna.[/b]

The buna are the oldest life forms on the planet and represent the warrior and ruling class of builders. [b]They are statuesque, have four arms, great physical strength and natural armor deriving from the rocky material their skin is made of. [/b]Their chrome plating depends on the rocks the souls come from, and it is said that it changes according to their mood and age.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/30d911f38bfa091c75c2c8a2d5c7bfe83a8221c4.png[/img]

Each young Buna must show their pride by leaving the village alone and defeating a large number of destroyers. The higher the value of the hunt, the higher the rank they will be entrusted with upon their return. For this reason, many young Buna in search of glory venture into very dangerous places, and it is not uncommon for many to never return.

[b]The wisest and oldest of Buna are called Maqalat. [/b]Their task is to keep alive the memories and traditions of its inhabitants by engraving the surface of the Dhakiras,  the ancestral stones encompassing the eternal memory of Gryja.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/707586b71b530d38bc65a72ed31b14c55089d81e.png[/img]

Their writing ritual takes place in extremely extended times, and their compositions can take hundreds of years. They spend their time absorbed on the slopes of the highest peaks, gazing at the sky in a constant trance. 

All Maqalat are deaf and dumb, as theirs is the language of the stars and the universe, and their consciences communicate transcending the order imposed by ordinary mortals.

[b]That’s all for today. Keep following us to discover many other exciting details on the Universe of Batora: Lost Haven and don’t forget to add Batora: Lost Haven to your wishlist![/b]

notes.title: Bringing Mila to life: Character Design and Inspiration
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/f6a332f9e127f5b5647867f072e3877d678d3204.jpg[/img]

Dreaming up a lifelike and relatable character, bringing it to life, and witnessing how it shapes up as part of the whole story is quite a challenging and meaningful experience.

As we have shown for Avril’s character design, this process requires a lot of in-depth analysis, creative effort and, why not, also a stroke of luck with finding inspiration. After all, the greatest ideas often spark at the most unexpected moments!

[b]Today we move on to the design of Mila, Avril’s best friend, to see how we brought her to life![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/fa946c30b6513e7bc62a31e64936b7408f862794.jpg[/img]

[b]Mila is a full-fledged companion character[/b] and, as such, designing her demanded a delicate balancing act between conveying emotions, in terms of fostering the bond we want the player to build with her, and ensure functionality. 

Mila joins Avril in her journey from the very beginning and, though not physically present in every step of the quest, [b]she plays an essential role all along.[/b]

Always looking on the bright side of life but never without a touch of sarcasm, Mila exudes an incredible charisma. She is friendly, confident, and, above all, brave and loyal: she is not the chosen one but still takes up the challenge and gives Avril the strength to overcome the most dreadful obstacles. 

When our main character feels like throwing in the towel, it’s Mila who reminds her what brought them this far and calls on her tireless commitment to save the Earth. Does this remind you of something? 

If you are a fan of [b]Lord of the Rings[/b], you may notice a degree of similarity to the relationship between the two hobbits [b]Samwise Gamgee [b]and [/b]Frodo Baggins[/b] and it’s no coincidence!

As [b]Gaetano Caltabiano, the Art Director of Batora: Lost Haven[/b] states [i]“The bond that ties Mila and Avril together is modeled on that of Frodo and Sam. The latter proved himself to be Frodo's closest and most dependable companion, always pushing him further on his quest, and so will Mila.”[/i]

However, we must highlight the fact that there’s no trace of any master and servant dynamics in the relationship between Avril and Mila and any references to the British Army’s batmans as in Tolkien’s masterpiece.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/39f8cb43c1cc0167625612aef26aa4d05d22baec.jpg[/img]

Once we laid down the foundations of the relationship between the two girls, we moved forward in the research of relevant references to better define Mila’s identity.

It may seem like an odd pairing but the two main references for the design of her character were [b]Mushu from Mulan[/b] for his personality and [b]Rue from The Hunger Games[/b] for her appearance and vibes!

Just like Mushu, Mila is fearless and has a snarky attitude, she supports her companion no matter what and gives her valuable advice, sharing a view from a different perspective. 

On the other hand, her kind nature and bravery is a trait she shares with [b]Rue from The Hunger Games[/b], Katniss Everdeen’s ally. Actually, the physical appearance of Mila is strongly inspired by the actress who plays the role of Rue,[b] Amandla Stenberg[/b]. Her aesthetic and expressiveness are indeed strikingly similar to that of the American actress and singer!

Last but not least, we also added a bit of the badass attitude of Michonne from The Walking Dead. Michonne is indeed extremely responsible and resourceful and somehow represents the direction in which Mila is heading: from reckless teenager to determined, brave young woman.

With all this in mind, [b]Borislav Mitkov[/b], former Assassin’s Creed Concept Artist who, as previously told, joined the project with the post of Character Concept Artist, finally brought the character of Mila to life. 

This is the result of his study:
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/2e94189cc11e17bf510c0608fd1f5631d8e9fb73.jpg[/img]

As for the outfit, the aim was to match and highlight the bubbly personality of Mila. Fashion and colorful, it draws inspiration from Korean and London streetwear. They both contain elements from punk, sportswear, and international styles, from California skate and surf culture to the Japanese Harajuku fashion.[b] The headscarf, in particular, is Mila’s trademark. [/b]

From what we’ve seen so far, one thing's for sure: everyone needs a friend like Mila! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/c0b6d7cddadd3436ed450e95e19d0fd35efca996.jpg[/img]

The complementary personalities of Avril and Mila, combined with their determination and dedication, will make their friendship even stronger and will prove to be invincible!

You’ve most likely read more than once that Avril is the main character of Batora: Lost Haven. Yet, we still haven’t told you much about her, so [b]let’s get to know Avril a little bit better today! [/b]

[b]Avril is a sixteen-year-old girl [/b]who lived her life to the fullest, except for the natural struggles a teenager has to deal with.

She didn’t like studying very much, actually, she has always been a bit of a maverick. Definitely not a bookworm, she has always preferred climbing trees and get into trouble with her friend Mila to any other quiet activity.

That was before the outbreak of a war completely changed her life and obscured most of the planet Earth. Now, Avril, forced to live in a dark place, among chaos and anarchy, is no longer the same girl she used to be and that you’d never have called a natural-born hero.

[b]She is the only one who, with her physical and mental powers, can attempt to save the Earth from oblivion. Come hell or high water[/b]. 

Along her path made of development and growth, Avril will travel from one planet to another, uncovering bigger and bigger secrets as the universe’s condition becomes more unstable and heavy. 

[b]She will soon find out that there is nor black or white, nor good or evil:[/b] there are decisions and these imply consequences leading to multiple outcomes.

notes.title: Shaping up the universe of Batora: Lost Haven: Gryja’s World-building.
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/91e7ff6fb149c4d457451edc0c135c37bfe3744c.png[/img]

The time has come for you to discover more about how the colorful and mesmerizing worlds of Batora: Lost Haven have come to life! 

In this first entry, we’ll focus on the main features and early steps in the design of the first planet: Gryja.

[b]The starting point for world-building in the game[/b] lies in the constant effort to give each of the planets Avril visits its own intriguing and distinctive identity. 

As she travels across the universe to develop and acquire the necessary physical and mental powers to save the Earth, Avril will move around [b]4 different planets[/b] with the most diverse environments. She will have to survive under multiple, sometimes even extreme, conditions!

First of all, [b]the uniqueness of each planet stems from the elemental force that it guards. [/b]

[b]The four elements of earth, air, water, and fire are the foundations of life in Batora: Lost Haven[/b] and the main principles that allow for cosmic balance: the planet of Gryja represents earth, Huav water, Mahdzam air, and Lume fire.

Second, but no less important, the different creatures that inhabit these four worlds are inspired by real human cultures. 

This does not just influence their appearance but also how the place they live in is depicted: coming across architectural and cultural elements from all over the world, past and present, is a constant in the game.

It’s not a secret that a core concept underlying the game is the sense of union, harmony, and sharing between different populations and cultures as an essential condition to save the Earth from near doom. 

Last but not least, following the logic of classic RPGs, [b]they are composed of separate explorable regions, with completely different environments from one another.[/b]

[b]With this in mind, let’s see how we shaped the world of Gryja![/b]

[b]GRYJA 

The planet of the Earth Element[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/4a3212cdacaea362a1343e3768926edeb8d2a5e2.jpg[/img]

Gryja is a rocky and desert planet, forged by recurrent earthquakes, defined as Gryjaquakes, which harbors forms of life generated from the earth’s elemental essence. 

When we came to design this first world, we started by taking inspiration from existing planets. In this case, from Mercury, a rocky, terrestrial planet with a solid, cratered surface. 

Much like we wanted Gryja to be!

In particular, as we aimed at emphasizing the widely varying geology within it, we built the color palette on the images obtained by the MESSENGER spacecraft in 2008.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/ced4afd43dab54ad46824f9ba6ea54f865544ffd.png[/img]
[i]Source: NASA/ Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory/ Carnegie Institution of Washington[/i]


These colors were not what Mercury would look like to the human eye but rather enhanced the chemical, mineralogical, and physical differences between the rocks that make up its surface. 

This explains why, despite Gryja’s settings being mainly dry and desertic,[b] its predominant colors are acidic! 
[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/fdb99640cbd5511a22b59f5a095a0383300efb7b.jpg[/img]

For their design of its inhabitants, which also influences the settings, we draw inspiration from the indigenous populations of [b]Himba of Namibia[/b] and the [b]“Mudmen” of Papua New Guinea’s Asaro tribe.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/39fe30132dd76a95538d36f3bb1c272ef3f22bba.jpg[/img]

Strong and brave, the creatures that live in Gryja range from nearly sentient to superior beings and are all made of the same material that envelops the entire planet. They worship nature, both as a creator and a destroyer.

That’s all for now. [b]Keep following us to discover many other exciting details on the Universe of Batora: Lost Haven![/b]

notes.title: Bringing Avril to life: Character Design and Inspiration
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/b8fae8c0b26161d34e5c4b3f33ca7eb4816d3a12.jpg[/img]

Character design is way more than the visual representation of a character; it’s about bringing them to life by fleshing out their mood, personality, and motivation through their look and feel. 

[b]That’s why we want you to look in a bit more detail at the first steps in turning Avril into a flesh-and-blood character![/b]

When we came to designing Batora: Lost Haven’s protagonist, the aim was to combine the four leading characters of the book [i]Batora[/i], from which the video game draws inspiration, into[b] a single, strong female main character who could take on major challenges on her own.[/b] It’s with this objective in mind that we got to Avril’s identity.

The next step of the creative process was then the research of references to gather and brainstorm visual details from comic books, mangas, and movie characters who could somehow be similar to the way we imagined her.

From the anatomy to her facial expressions, from the physical poses to the clothes she wears, her appearance had to accurately mirror her personality, attitude, and backstory. 

Despite our commitment, however, [b]finding relevant references was no easy task at all![/b]

As you can imagine, [b]the greatest ideas and inspirations often spark at the most unexpected times,[/b] and this is exactly what happened to Gaetano Caltabiano, the Art Director of  Batora: Lost Haven.

Gaetano already had a clear idea of who Avril was going to be, but it was only while he was watching [i]Spiderman Far From Home[/i] that he saw Michelle Jones – played by the actress Zendaya – and had his eureka moment: [i]“Zendaya Is Avril, She Is Her, She Is Her!”[/i]

For him, the two had so much in common that he immediately thought that was the way Avril should look like![b] Avril is indeed just as curious, observant and a bit of a shy loner as Michelle Jones and they share the very same dry sense of humor as well! [/b]

Of course, they are also different. Unlike MJ, Avril is a little bit ditsy but that doesn’t make her any less! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/04899f865cfc681ead3feeffdfe7de24bdd9b8d3.png[/img]

Once the foundations of the character were laid down, we moved forward in the research and soon found out that [b]Avril also had some common traits with Katniss Everdeen from Hunger Games: they are both strong, resourceful sixteen-year-old girls[/b] who demonstrate their perseverance by staying true to themselves and facing danger with open arms.

At this stage, it was time for the Art Director to pass the torch to[b] Borislav Mitkov, [/b]former Assassin’s Creed Concept Artist [b]who joined Batora: Lost Haven project with the post of Character Concept Artist.
[/b]
Borislav gathered all the references, samples, and features and turn them into reality to finally bring Avril to life. This is the result of his study:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/8d5b9d8c06ac03090d9ed3723841b5b7fbff1dce.jpg[/img]

[b]Then, the only thing left was the design of an outfit that could match both her personality and mission!

As for the clothing, we took cues from the vibrant color schemes and detailed line work of Alphonse Mucha[/b] to style a polished, bright, and colorful Sci-fi outfit specifically created to assist Avril on her mission: the suit and boots enable her to resist the gravitational pull and the weather conditions of all the planets she visits, while her endless-capacity quantum backpack can store everything she collects.

Another powerful means that enables Avril to survive under the most extreme and diverse conditions of the universe – and her most distinguishing feature as well – is [b]the symbol on her forehead. [/b]

Representing a stylized sun and moon, it is the point from which her mental power is released and symbolizes the equilibrium between opposite and complementary principles, thanks to which the universe came into being and continues to exist. 

As a woman, [b]Avril is deeply connected to the concepts of origin and rebirth[/b] evoked by ancient goddesses such as Iset and Freya. Furthermore, the mark on her forehead recalls that of the deities of Shiva and Buddha.

One last tidbit: the symbol of the sun, in its Native American declination, can also be found into the hilt and tip of Avril’s sword!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/fe1ae05cd1fd8f554bb805c64216fd686d580429.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39697761/a310f4526ad9ebad0220bbd931d4c6250df993db.jpg[/img]

No need to say, the design process of Avril has been long and demanding.  Many things have changed along the way but[b] our purpose has always been crystal clear from the very beginning: [/b]

As the only one who can restore the universal balance, Avril had to encompass cultural elements and archetypes from all over the world to [b]reinforce the sense of union and sharing required to save the Earth from near doom![/b]

notes.title: Meet Batora: Lost Haven
notes.notes:
What only a day ago was still a new, undisclosed [b]Stormind Games’[/b] project, has finally been revealed: [b]the brand new story-driven action RPG Batora: Lost Haven![/b]

Presented yesterday through [b]IGN’s worldwide exclusive[/b], Batora: Lost Haven follows Avril –  a regular 16-year old girl, not a natural-born hero – as she realizes, after losing everything she cares for, that [b]she is the only one who can save a devastated planet Earth from oblivion. [/b]
This is how her interplanetary adventure starts: along this journey, she will visit colorful and mysterious planets - all with the eye-filling visuals inspired by the [b]Retro Sci-Fi Art of the 1950s[/b] - and meet the most intriguing characters in the whole universe! 

And, above all, she will learn that [b]every choice has a consequence.[/b]

Seeing notable collaborations with award-winning writer [b]Anne Toole[/b] (Horizon Zero Dawn, The Witcher, Days Gone), [b]Ron Fish[/b] - composer of the soundtracks of God of War and the Warner Bros Arkham Series, and former Assassin’s Creed Concept Artist [b]Borislav Mitkov[/b], Batora: Lost Haven is [b]a fast-paced adventure rich in plot twists, emotions and adrenaline,[/b] that will allow you to [b]shape your own story as it unfolds[/b], challenging your strategy skills - this game will require you to think fast and react even faster!
